In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical constraints and limitations imposed upon the design of high speed, large capacity, high performance, interconnection networks.
the design of high speed packet passing interconnection networks for use in multiprocessors.
the development of interconnection networks which will provide high speed communication between processing elements in multiprocessor architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physical design of a network centered architecture will be a very challenging problem.
the physical constraints of interconnection networks are very severe.
the physical design of an interconnection network can be made such that it does not limit the clock frequency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physical design of a network centered multiprocessors is not trivial and that the performance of such a multiprocessor will be limited by the interconnection network.
we believe that the interconnection network is a major problem in multiprocessor design and that the design of such networks is not well understood.
a network based on the design presented in this paper is feasible but that the clock frequencies which can be used are limited by physical considerations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of interconnects for large-scale multiprocessors is a difficult problem.
it is important to consider physical constraints in the design and performance evaluation of network based multiprocessor architectures.
interconnection networks are not a panacea for the performance problem.
